To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the total reward of the system is increased when the uncertainty of information is small, and (2) when the uncertainty of the information is small, the agent tends to choose the behavior of cooperation, and when the uncertainty of infor- mation is large, the agent tends not to choose the behavior.

(1) the agent system based on Hogg-Hubermans model can achieve higher rewards than a system based on the replicator dynamics model and (2) the agent system can select the behavior that maximizes the rewards.

we found that the total rewards of whole system in our agent system based on Hogg-Hubermann model are larger than those in a system in which agents select a behavior based on a simple rule, and that the behavior of an agent in our agent system is more cooperative than that in the system in which agents follow a simple rule.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hogg-Hubbeman model is a good way to model the social behavior of the agents, but the agents should be given a chance to choose the strategy that is more profitable to them.
the agent system based on Hogg-Hubermans model can be used for a system with a large number of agents and that the agent behavior is affected by the uncertainty of information and the time delay.
the agent based on Hogg-Hubermann model can improve the total rewards of a system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hogg-Hubbeman model can be applied to a social system and that the agent can choose the appropriate strategy by considering uncertainty of information and the time delay.
the agent's selection of behavior depends on the agent's behavior in the previous period.
the agent system can be applied to the real world and the results of this work are expected to contribute to the understanding of the mechanism of the social dilemma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the agent can select the cooperative behavior in the tragedy game by the Hogg-Hubbeman model.
the agent system with a collaborative tendency is able to achieve a higher total reward than the agent system without the collaborative tendency in the tragedy game.

the agents with the collaborative behavior can obtain the total rewards more than those with the competitive behavior, and the agents with the cooperative behavior can obtain the higher reward than those with the collaborative behavior.
